requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: Executor installed createrepo_c, downloaded a package (tree) into /srv/localrepo, ran createrepo_c to build repodata, stood up a systemd-managed python http.server on port 8080 bound to the node IP, opened the firewall port, and verified HTTP 200 responses for repomd.xml and the RPM both before and after a reboot (service remained active/enabled).

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while usual remote repositories are unreachable
requirements.summary: Executor forced mirrors.centos.org to resolve to localhost via /etc/hosts, confirmed dnf makecache failed for baseos/appstream with a curl connection error (remote repos unreachable), then successfully installed the 'tree' package with --disablerepo="*" --enablerepo="local", verified via rpm -q, and afterward restored /etc/hosts and confirmed remote repos worked again.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart healthy state, restart, distinct post-restart boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state)
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot state captured boot id 4d340bf4..., service active/enabled, package installed, HTTP 200 (cmd-164a2d9d2bb347a7). systemctl reboot was issued and the connection dropped/reconnected (cmd-eb3d91d80b58433a, cmd-2f681f559c7b4702, cmd-64c7117c53d94e30). Post-reboot boot id changed to 6c85995a... with a fresh uptime (cmd-6bd4969884ae4312), and the local repo service, installed package, HTTP endpoint, and a fresh reinstall from the local repo were all verified working again (cmd-1398439c30404380). This is corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (before: 4d340bf4..., after: 6c85995a...).

overall_summary: The executor successfully built and served a local package repository (createrepo_c + systemd-managed http.server on port 8080, firewall opened) and demonstrated installing the 'tree' package from it with --enablerepo=\"local\" while confirming genuine unreachability of the real CentOS mirrors via a controlled /etc/hosts redirect, which was cleanly reverted afterward. The executor also independently ran the node-restart evidence protocol on node1: a healthy pre-restart baseline, an issued systemctl reboot, a distinct post-restart boot id, and full recovery of the repo service, installed package, and HTTP access were all directly observed. No unnecessary or unresolved destructive mutations were found; only minor /tmp log residue was left behind.
limitations: The executor's structured final report and selected-evidence list were placeholder/test values ('test', 'cmd-1') and did not reference any real command IDs, so this evaluation relied entirely on the raw command timeline and fixed lifecycle snapshots rather than the executor's own evidence citations.

cmd-84b6eb6239f34573 (find for the tree rpm) returned no output, which is unexplained but appears inconsequential since the package and repo file were independently confirmed present via other commands.
Executor evidence item 1 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-1

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were bounded and purposeful: the /etc/hosts edit used to simulate remote-repo unreachability (cmd-9e78713dc2284951) was fully reverted from a saved backup (cmd-0d46f4f1cdfe4149); the systemd unit, firewall port opening, and local.repo file are retained but are direct, intended artifacts of the task requirement to serve and use a local repository. The reboot (cmd-eb3d91d80b58433a) was a deliberate, expected action for the restart-evidence protocol with no destructive side effects observed. Minor residue: several log files were left under /tmp (createrepo.log, createrepo2.log, createrepo_install.log, dl.log, install.log, makecache.log, makecache2.log, reboot.log, visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot) — low-severity clutter, not damaging or security-relevant. No failed services, no unsafe exposure beyond the intentionally opened repo port, and no unrevoked destructive changes were found.
